text:
Through the old neighborhood, where the shutters
Of little houses hide secret lusts
When the cruel star furiously strikes
City and fields, roofs and seedbeds,

I wish to practice my fantastic fencing,
Sniffing out in corners the chances of rhyme,
Stumbling over syllables as over paving stones,
Perhaps finding verses I dreamed long ago.

That nourishing father, who flees chloroses,
Wakes verses and roses in the fields;
Makes grief evaporate into ether
By filling brains and beehives with honey.

It is he who erases years for the man on crutches
And makes him festive like lovely girls,
And orders the grain to ripen and grow
In the immortal womb that longs to flower.

When, like a poet, he descends into cities,
He ennobles the lot of meanest things,
And enters like a king, without train or pomp,
Into royal houses and hospitals alike.

translation.title: The Sun
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Baudelaire’s French original.
